title: What I Learned When My Best Friend Moved Overseas
script: Narrator: [warmly] When Vina told me she was moving overseas for a new job, I congratulated her warmly, although inside, I felt a strange sense of panic.
Narrator: We had been best friends since university, seeing each other almost every week, so I couldn't imagine what our friendship would become without that.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I assumed distance would slowly kill our closeness, the way it seemed to happen with other old friendships I had watched fade.
Narrator: So, before she left, we sat down together and actually planned how we wanted to stay close, instead of just hoping it would happen naturally.
Narrator: [carefully] We planned a Sunday call, but agreed to move or skip it without guilt when work, health, or time zones made it difficult.
Narrator: The first few calls felt forced, because we were both adjusting, and there was an odd new distance between our voices.
Narrator: [reflective] But we kept showing up anyway, even on weeks when neither of us had much interesting to say.
Narrator: Slowly, something shifted. We started sharing small details again, what we cooked, who annoyed us at work, ordinary things that used to feel too small to mention.
Narrator: [gently] I also started sending short voice messages during my day, little updates that didn't need an immediate reply.
Narrator: She began doing the same, and somehow, those small messages made the huge distance between our cities feel much smaller.
Narrator: [honestly] Last month, she visited home for two weeks, and I worried it would feel awkward seeing each other in person again.
Narrator: It didn't. We picked up exactly where we left off, laughing within minutes, as though barely any time had passed at all.
Narrator: [encouraging] I learned that distance changes a friendship, but mutual effort and flexible expectations can keep a meaningful connection alive.
Narrator: Our friendship is one example, not a rule for everyone. We both initiate contact, respect delayed replies, and adjust the plan when life changes.

quiz.question: How did the narrator feel when Vina announced she was moving overseas?
quiz.explanation: She congratulated Vina warmly but felt a strange sense of panic inside.

quiz.question: What did the narrator and Vina agree to do before Vina left?
options: Never contact each other to avoid pain
Have one video call every Sunday
quiz.explanation: They agreed on one video call every Sunday, no matter how busy they became.

quiz.question: How did the first few calls feel?
options: Forced, with an odd new distance between their voices
quiz.explanation: The first few calls felt forced, with an odd new distance between their voices.

quiz.question: What else did the narrator start doing besides calling?
options: Sending short voice messages during the day
quiz.explanation: She started sending short voice messages with little updates that didn't need an immediate reply.

quiz.question: What does the narrator conclude about distance and friendship?
options: Distance only ends friendships nobody chooses to protect on purpose
Friendship requires living in the same city
Video calls are unnecessary for real friendship
quiz.explanation: She concludes distance only ends the friendships that nobody chooses to protect on purpose.

quiz.question: Why do the friends plan before the move?
options: They expect the job to fail
They want realistic ways to maintain contact
They want to end other friendships
quiz.explanation: Connection becomes easier with shared expectations.

quiz.question: What problem appears with a fixed weekly call?
options: Work and time-zone changes sometimes make Sunday impossible
quiz.explanation: A routine needs flexibility rather than guilt.

quiz.question: Why are small voice messages useful?
options: They share ordinary life without requiring an immediate reply

quiz.question: What does mutual effort look like?
options: Both initiate contact and adjust when life changes
They measure equal minutes each week
quiz.explanation: Fairness is shared but not mechanically identical.

quiz.question: What is the revised conclusion?
options: Every distant friendship must remain close
Distance changes friendship, but flexible care can preserve it
An ocean changes nothing at all
quiz.explanation: The lesson is hopeful without making a universal promise.
